capture.final_message:
View filters as upward-closed families of sets.

- For the first conjunct, unfold `Filter.map`: by definition, \(t\in\operatorname{map}(m,f)\) exactly when \(m^{-1}(t)\in f\).

- For `comap`, use its membership characterization:
  \[
  A\in\operatorname{comap}(f,l)
  \iff \exists T\in l,\ f^{-1}(T)\subseteq A.
  \]
  Taking \(A=s^{c}\), use the set-theoretic equivalence
  \[
  f^{-1}(T)\subseteq s^{c}
  \iff T\subseteq (f''s)^{c}.
  \]
  Upward closure of \(l\) then gives
  \[
  s^{c}\in\operatorname{comap}(f,l)
  \iff (f''s)^{c}\in l.
  \]

- The proposition on the other side of the outer `Iff` is the basic generator property of `comap`: if \(t\in g\), then \(m^{-1}(t)\in\operatorname{comap}(m,g)\), witnessed by \(t\) itself.

Thus prove both universally quantified propositions independently and conclude their equivalence. No injectivity or surjectivity is needed; using the complement of the image, rather than the image of the complement, is the key point.
